newsitem.title: USA: PointCast may sell stock in IPO this year-CEO.
newsitem.headline: PointCast may sell stock in IPO this year-CEO.

text.p: PointCast Inc., a pioneer of Internet direct broadcasting technology, said it may sell stock to the public this year and also denied recent rumours that it was in talks to be acquired.
"Our intent is not to remain private," said PointCast Chief Executive Officer Christopher Hassett.

"An IPO is definitely a possibility in the near future," he said, referring to a possible initial public offering. He would not give details but said the spring and summer were "reasonable timeframes."
Hassett also denied recent rumours swirling in the industry that the company was in talks to be acquired by News Corp. Ltd.
"That's a rumour. There are no facts behind that," he said, adding that PointCast was always talking with media companies since many are partners in providing news to the PointCast Network.

PointCast, based in Cupertino, Calif., has developed so-called push technology with a network that delivers news and other content directly to a subscriber's desktop computer. That way, users do not have to scan scores of Web sites looking for news, stock quotes, sports scores and other data.
The company has many big media companies as its content providers and partners, including Times Mirror Co., the New York Times Co. and Reuters Holdings Plc.

Last week, rumours were swirling that Rupert Murdoch's News Corp., which owns Fox News, TV Guide, The New York Post and 20th Century Fox, was going to acquire PointCast for $300 million to $400 million.

"I can tell you flat out that there is zero percent chance of that, that's just not going to happen," Hassett said. "It's just not factual." He also said merging with Microsoft Corp. also rumoured, was not a possibility.
"Microsoft is a partner of ours, we are not in acquisition discussions with Microsoft," Hassett said.
He said PointCast's investment banker, Morgan Stanley, has provided financing in private security sales and other transactions.
"They would do our IPO," Hassett said. He declined to provide any financial details on the company.
